calls.head: Crash the net vs. bombs away
calls.body: The Rangers get in close, but the Blackhawks mostly shoot from distance. The Rangers are one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Rangers to do more of their damage around the net.

calls.beyond: The Rangers are one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 178 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 117 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

surprises.head: The Rangers buried Chicago in shots
surprises.body: Chicago takes fewer shots than almost anyone. Even by those standards, this was lopsided: the Rangers took 58 of the 80 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, the Rangers would expect about 54%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: Mangiapane has two goals as the Blackhawks edge the Rangers
paras: Andrew Mangiapane struck first for the Blackhawks on the power play early in the first, and Matt Rempe and Dillon Boucher dropped the gloves midway through the period. Mika Zibanejad made it 1-1 for the Rangers on the power play late in the period, with J.T. Miller picking up his 500th NHL assist on the goal. Mangiapane scored again on the power play with just under a minute left in the period to put the Hawks ahead for good.

The Rangers had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Rangers win about six in ten. Spencer Knight was the difference, stopping 30 of 31. Dylan Garand stopped 8 of 10 for the Rangers. The Blackhawks moved to 10-14-2, still last in the Central, while the Rangers fell to 13-11-1, fourth in the Metropolitan.
